record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Given a matrix A in CP_n, determine a completely positive factorization of A, meaning a representation A = B B^T in which B is an entrywise nonnegative matrix.

evidence.quote: The basic open problem is: given A ∈ CPn, determine a cp-factorization of A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real symmetric n×n matrix A is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative (not necessarily square) matrix B such that A = B B^T; the set of all such matrices is denoted CP_n. A representation A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative is called a completely positive factorization (cp-factorization) of A.

Problem: Devise a general procedure that, given an arbitrary matrix A ∈ CP_n, explicitly produces a completely positive factorization A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative. Equivalently, given a completely positive matrix, compute an explicit nonnegative factor B realizing it.
artifact.status_search_result: The general task of computing a cp-factorization is known to be NP-hard. Numerous algorithms have been proposed (polyhedral inner approximation methods, alternating projections, simplex-type rational factorization, Riemannian smoothing, iterative projected gradient, alternating minimization), and these work for matrices in the interior of CP_n or with special structure (e.g. cp-rank 3, circular, acyclic, certain graph structures). However, no algorithm is known that reliably produces a cp-factorization for every matrix in CP_n, particularly for matrices on the boundary, so the problem remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Building a completely positive factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm based on projections onto polyhedral inner approximations of CP_n; factorizes interior matrices but generally fails for boundary matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Existing methods handle interior of CP_n but fail in general.

status_evidence.title: A factorization method for completely positive matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Nonconvex feasibility approach via alternating projections to compute cp-factorizations.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic/feasibility methods exist but no complete algorithm.

status_evidence.title: A simplex algorithm for rational cp-factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Simplex-like algorithm for rational cp-factorization, with applications to integral 2x2 case.

status_evidence.title: Computing the completely positive factorization via alternating minimization
